text:
support-eng: FYI we just got an escalated ticket from AcmeCorp — p99 latency jumped from ~1.2s -> 4.8s for their streaming generate endpoint starting ~08:12 UTC. They say it correlates with a spike in multi-tenant burst traffic. Ticket: TKT-4219.
support-eng: Attaching initial graphs: CPU ok, GPU util steady, but kv/prefix_cache miss_rate jumped from 6% -> 68% and p95 also inched up. Suspect prefix cache thrash/warmup.
alex: Thanks — can you paste the query pattern and a short repro?
support-eng: Example request they provided: `POST /v1/generate` body includes prompt with tenant-specific prefixes + long conversation history. Repro curl they ran: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rw1-large","input":"<tenant:acme> \nUser: ..."}'``` They also said spikes line up with many small unique prefixes (customer id + ephemeral session tokens).
maria: That lines up w/ previous prefix-key-entropy issues. If keys include ephemeral session tokens we get very high cardinality and frequent eviction. Do we have per-tenant partitioning enabled for this cluster?
jamal: Cluster config shows partitioning disabled for this pool (defaults). Eviction policy is LRU with a max_keys of 200k, TTL 10m. With high-cardinality prefixes LRU oscillates and warms poorly.
kyra: Can we confirm the runtime logs for cache evictions? I pulled `/var/log/runtime/prefix_cache.log` from one affected pod: ```[08:11:53] INFO prefix_cache:evict key=tenant:acme:session:xyz reason=capacity
[08:11:54] INFO prefix_cache:miss key=tenant:acme:session:abc
[08:11:55] WARN prefix_cache:hot_eviction_oscillation window=15s count=92``` That matches thrash.
sre-oncall: Immediate mitigation options? Increase capacity or change eviction behavior. We could bump max_keys to 400k for the impacted node group and redeploy config. That buys short-term relief.
alex: Short-term bump is fine but we should avoid naive long-term. Proposed medium-term mitigations: 1) Normalize cache keys to strip ephemeral tokens (if safe) 2) Prefer segmented caches: per-tenant or per-model namespaces with quotas 3) Change eviction to SLRU (segmented LRU) so we protect stable prefixes from being evicted by one-off keys.
maria: Also add proactive warmup: on new session creation, prefetch prefix KV for the model's usual system prompts and recent history. That reduces cold-miss penalty.
jamal: I can sketch a rollout: A) Add a normalization layer to keygen that removes / hashes ephemeral session ids for prefix cache keys (config flag `cache.normalize_session_ids=true`) B) Add SLRU implementation behind feature flag `cache.slrue=true` C) For immediate customer relief, increase `cache.max_keys` to 400k on pool `rw-large-us-west-2` and set `cache.eviction_burst_limit=50` to damp oscillation.
kyra: Need to be careful: normalizing could cause cross-session pollution if sessions intentionally separate state. We'll coordinate with support and AcmeCorp about what qualifies as ephemeral. Must ship behind opt-in per-tenant.
support-eng: AcmeCorp gave permission to try normalization for their tenant only. They want a canary.
alex: Good. Action plan: 1) jamal will deploy a per-tenant normalization toggle and apply to AcmeCorp as a canary 2) jamal will bump pool max_keys for rw-large-us-west-2 as emergency config 3) maria will add warmup hook in session-creation flow 4) kyra will add metrics/traces for cache_miss_ratio by normalized_prefix and by raw_key so we can see effect. 5) Create rollback plan to revert normalization and max_keys changes.
jamal: I'll open a PR with small changes and a k8s job to bump config via configmap for the pool. Repro steps for SRE to validate before canary: ```# run on staging with synthetic high-cardinality prefixes
for i in {1..10000}; do curl -s -X POST $STAGE_URL/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d "{\"model\":\"rw1-large\",\"input\":\"<tenant:acme> session:$RANDOM prompt: hi\"}" & done
# then check metrics
kubectl logs -l app=runtime -c prefix-cache | grep miss | wc -l
promql: sum(rate(prefix_cache_miss_total[1m])) by (pod)
```
kyra: I'll add dashboards and an alert: `prefix_cache_miss_ratio > 0.2 for 5m` for critical deployments and a synthetic canary that runs the above script once/min.
alex: Also add a fallback to model variant with shorter context if miss rate remains high and latency SLOs are in danger. That preserves UX.
sre-oncall: For the immediate emergency I've applied a config bump on rw-large-us-west-2 and restarted 3 pods at 08:35 UTC. Early signals: miss_rate dropped from 68% -> 14% and p99 back down to ~1.5s. But we need the canary to validate normalization effect long-term.
maria: I'll prepare the warmup PR and a small benchmark showing token-rate improvement when warmup present.
jamal: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/1139 — includes feature flag, per-tenant toggle, and stress test. Request reviews from @alex and @kyra.
kyra: Reviewing now. Also adding a metric `prefix_cache_eviction_oscillation_count` exposed as a gauge to help detect thrash automatically.
support-eng: Noted — I've updated ticket TKT-4219 with the mitigation steps and timeline. AcmeCorp acknowledges and will monitor.
alex: Nice work. Follow-ups: - schedule canary for tenant next Tue 09:00 UTC - add runbook note under docs/cache-troubleshooting for operators - decide on default for new clusters (SLRU + sane max_keys).
deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime-configmap update for rw-large-us-west-2 by jamal (change: cache.max_keys=400000) at 08:34:12 UTC.
jamal: I'll coordinate the canary next Tue and prepare rollback playbook (how to disable normalization and revert max_keys).
